sessions.title: Help me understand Service level, including the metric d

messages.text: Help me understand Service level, including the metric definition and the visible values.

sourceContext.comparisonWindow: Compared with the same through-noon period across the preceding five operating days

messages.text: Service level is the percentage metric shown for each queue, expressed from 0% to 100%. In this view, the displayed values are: Sales 75%, Billing 68%, Account Services 79%, Returns 82%, and Technical Support 85%. The visible average is 77.8%. The chart also shows a target of 80%, so the average is 2.2 percentage points below target. The reporting window is today through noon, with comparison intended against the same through-noon period across the preceding five operating days; no comparison values are visible here. The source does not provide a more specific business-rule definition—for example, the response-time threshold or denominator—so those details cannot be inferred from the displayed data.
Explain how Service level is calculated if the underlying business rule is available

sourceContext.comparisonWindow: Compared with the same through-noon period across the preceding five operating days

messages.text:
The underlying business rule is not available in the supplied source, so the exact Service level formula cannot be confirmed. In particular, the data does not specify the qualifying response-time threshold, what interactions belong in the denominator, or how exclusions and abandoned contacts are handled.

What can be confirmed from the artifact is that Service level is displayed as a percentage for each queue, and the visible average is calculated as the arithmetic mean of the five queue values:
(75% + 68% + 79% + 82% + 85%) ÷ 5 = 77.8%.

Thus, 77.8% is the mean of the displayed queue-level percentages—not a confirmed overall contact-weighted Service level. The chart target is 80%, making the displayed average 2.2 percentage points below target. The reporting window is today through noon.
suggestions: Provide the underlying business-rule documentation to determine the exact numerator and denominator.
Confirm whether the overall Service level should be contact-weighted rather than averaged across queues.

metrics.name: Abandoned
metrics.formula: Offered calls ended by the customer before answer.

metrics.name: Abandonment Rate
metrics.formula: Abandoned calls divided by offered calls, expressed as a percentage.

limitations: Queue abandonment is represented as distinct offered and abandoned calls per queue per day. Abandoned calls are a subset of offered calls.

artifacts.title: Agent Activity
artifacts.summary: Synthetic data: 100 source rows; 100 displayed rows.

metrics.name: Active agents
metrics.formula: Distinct agents with handling segments overlapping the reporting period.

metrics.name: Interactions
metrics.formula: Distinct customer interactions with matching handling segments. AI and human cohorts overlap for transferred interactions; cohort counts must not be added.

metrics.name: Handling minutes
metrics.formula: Handling-segment duration clipped to the reporting period, in minutes.

limitations: Agent Activity is represented by handling segments, not login or availability states.

artifacts.title: Queue Abandonment
artifacts.summary: Synthetic data: 5 source rows; 5 displayed rows. Abandonment Rate: 11.23 %.

briefings.title: Morning supervisor briefing
briefings.comparisonWindow: Compared with the equivalent period across the preceding five operating days
summary: Sales abandonment is 67% (+9 pts versus baseline)
Billing is 72% within target (−8 pts versus baseline)
Handoffs complete in 74% (−9 pts versus baseline)

widgets.title: Queue abandonment rate
widgets.explanation: Customers are leaving before an agent answers. Sales is the outlier in a five-queue comparison.
widgets.definition: Abandoned interactions ÷ offered interactions. Demo target: under 45%.
widgets.investigatePrompt: Investigate why Sales queue abandonment is rising and suggest staffing actions.

widgets.title: Service level
widgets.explanation: Billing missed the 80% service objective while volume stayed above its normal range.
widgets.definition: Interactions answered within the service threshold ÷ offered interactions. Demo target: 80%.
widgets.investigatePrompt: Investigate why Billing service level is below target and identify the drivers.

widgets.title: Agent acceptance rate
widgets.explanation: Jordan’s acceptance rate has declined for two comparable windows and needs a schedule or state review.
widgets.definition: Accepted offers ÷ offered interactions. Demo target: 85%.
widgets.investigatePrompt: Investigate declining agent acceptance and compare availability by agent.

widgets.title: Ring-no-answer rate
widgets.explanation: Ring-no-answer is elevated across two queues, suggesting missed alerts or availability-state issues.
widgets.definition: Ringing interactions not answered ÷ agent offers. Demo target: under 12%.
widgets.investigatePrompt: Investigate ring-no-answer increases by queue and agent.

widgets.title: Queue pressure and occupancy
widgets.explanation: High occupancy paired with rising wait pressure leaves little buffer for breaks or spikes.
widgets.definition: Active handling time ÷ staffed time. Demo target: 75–85%.
widgets.investigatePrompt: Compare queue pressure with agent occupancy and recommend capacity actions.

widgets.title: Agent time distribution
widgets.explanation: After-call work is taking a larger share of staffed time than usual for two agents.
widgets.definition: Minutes in a state ÷ total staffed minutes. Demo target: review after-call work above 25%.
widgets.investigatePrompt: Break down agent time by state and identify coaching opportunities.

widgets.title: Outbound campaign success
widgets.explanation: Renewals is below its campaign target while the other campaigns remain inside normal variation.
widgets.definition: Successful outbound outcomes ÷ completed outbound attempts. Demo target: 48%.
widgets.investigatePrompt: Investigate outbound campaign success rates and compare contact strategies.

widgets.title: Repeat-contact pressure
widgets.explanation: Returns customers are returning soon after resolution more often than in comparable periods.
widgets.definition: Customers with another interaction in seven days ÷ resolved customers. Demo target: under 20%.
widgets.investigatePrompt: Investigate repeat-contact pressure by queue and resolution outcome.

widgets.title: AI resolution quality
widgets.explanation: Synthetic extension: AI answers remain useful but quality fell on handoff-heavy topics.
widgets.definition: Composite resolution-quality score from completion, sentiment, and policy checks. Demo target: 85/100.
widgets.investigatePrompt: Investigate AI resolution quality and identify the topics needing improvement.

widgets.title: AI-to-human handoff health
widgets.explanation: Synthetic extension: customers are waiting longer after AI escalation and some context is incomplete.
widgets.definition: Completed human handoffs with conversation context ÷ AI escalation attempts. Demo target: 85%.
widgets.investigatePrompt: Investigate AI-to-human handoff health and find where handoffs are failing.

widgets.title: Interaction volume trend
widgets.explanation: A seven-day area chart is suited to showing a continuous volume trend and its daily shape.
widgets.definition: Daily interactions across the synthetic support operation.
widgets.investigatePrompt: Compare the daily volume trend by channel.

widgets.title: Handling-time relationship
widgets.finding: Satisfaction falls as handling time increases in this scenario.
widgets.explanation: The regression line summarizes the relationship between handling time and customer satisfaction across the synthetic queue sample.
widgets.definition: Synthetic observations are used to illustrate a linear trend, not causation.
widgets.investigatePrompt: Inspect the records behind this relationship.

widgets.title: Channel mix
widgets.finding: Digital channels represent the largest share of interactions.
widgets.explanation: A pie chart shows the composition of a small set of mutually exclusive interaction channels.
widgets.definition: Share of total synthetic interactions by channel.
widgets.investigatePrompt: Compare the channel mix over time.

widgets.title: Queue activity pattern
widgets.finding: Queue activity peaks around midday for Sales and Billing.
widgets.explanation: A heatmap compares intensity across hours and queues, making concentrated activity easy to find.
widgets.definition: Synthetic activity index by queue and hour.
widgets.investigatePrompt: Compare this activity pattern with queue abandonment.
